Islay, late November

Thursday 26 – Monday 30 November 2026 · based near Port Charlotte / Kilchoman

Arrive Thu ~15:30 Leave Mon on the 12:45 ferry Booked: Lagavulin cocktails, Sat 13:30 Jura day trip: Friday
Day by day What's on More to do Ferries Weather Open this weekend Eat & drink Walks & wildlife Check before you go

Day by day

Sunrise is ~08:25 and sunset ~16:00 all weekend, so each full day below is timed to fill the daylight — three to four concrete activities a day, with start times, durations and the drives between them. Evenings are for pubs and booked suppers.

Thursday26 November · arrive

Ferry in, settle in — then drinks and supper in Port Charlotte

  • 13:00–14:55 — Ferry, Kennacraig → Port Askaig (amended timetable). Check in 30 min before with a car, 10 min on foot; book ahead even as a foot passenger. Thursday night is the weekend's worst weather — heavy rain and 33 mph southerlies — so check CalMac service status before leaving for Kennacraig.
  • 15:00–16:00 — Drive Port Askaig → Port Charlotte (~1 hr) and check in. Sunset is 16:02, so this drive uses the last of the daylight.
  • 17:00–18:30 — Port Charlotte Hotel bar — settle in after the ferry day with Islay malts and Islay Ales on tap by the wood-burning fire. It's on Main Street in the village, so there's no drive in the dark and wet, and you're already in the right place for supper.
  • 18:45–20:15 — Supper at the Port Charlotte Hotel (evening meals 18:00–21:00) — book on 01496 850360. Lochindaal Hotel's bars are on the same street for a nightcap.

Forecast: PM light rain turning heavy overnight · 8°C, feels 2°C · rain 90% · SSE wind 30–33 mph · sunrise 08:21, sunset 16:02.

Friday27 November · Jura day trip

The only full day that fits for Jura — and the driest day

  • 09:45 — Leave Kilchoman / Port Charlotte for Port Askaig (~40 min). 10:30 ferry, Port Askaig → Feolin, then drive Feolin → Craighouse, ~8 miles / 20 min on the single-track shore road — watch for otters and deer. Arrive Craighouse ~10:55.
  • 11:00–12:15 — Corran Sands loop, 4 km (1 hr 15 min). The shore-and-river circuit from Big Corran, just north of Craighouse — white sand, views back to the Paps. Kept brisk to fit the later start.
  • 12:20–12:50 — Craighouse old pier (30 min). Deer Island Rum at the pier, Camella Crafts and the Whisky Island Gallery (open Fri 12:00–16:00), plus the community shop for supplies. No dated event was found on Jura for Fri 27 Nov.
  • 12:50–13:35 — Lunch in Craighouse: The Antlers Bakehouse & Bar / café (Sun–Fri 09:00–17:00) or the Jura Hotel pub (open Thu–Sat in November).
  • 13:45–15:45 — Drive north up the single-track coast road (2 hrs with stops). Craighouse → Tarbert → Inverlussa bay (15 min stop — the sheltered bay at the Lussa river mouth) → Ardlussa, where there's a brief shop stop at Lussa Gin (15 min, no tour — it's ~25 miles north of the Feolin ferry, so it only works as part of this drive) → the Barnhill turn-off, Orwell's house seen from the road only. Then straight back down the coast road to Craighouse — shorter stops than a full morning start would allow, but the whole route still fits in daylight.
  • 16:00–17:00 — Bothan Jura Wild Sauna, Big Corran / Craighouse (60 min) — if bookable: book ahead and confirm the slot before you go; it's on the way back through Craighouse. If no slot, use the hour in Craighouse instead and leave at the same time.
  • 17:15 — Leave Craighouse for Feolin (20 min). 17:45 ferry back to Port Askaig, then ~1 hr back to Port Charlotte for supper (Port Charlotte Hotel kitchen runs to 21:00).

Forecast: morning showers, then partly cloudy — the best day of the trip · 9°C, feels 3°C · rain 40%, 0.8 mm · SSW wind 12 mph · sunrise 08:23, sunset 16:01.

Saturday28 November · Lagavulin day

South-coast walks in the morning, your one booking at 13:30

  • 08:00–09:00 — Drive Port Charlotte → Ardbeg (~1 hr via Bowmore and Port Ellen) and park at Ardbeg. Saturday is by car throughout — everything below starts and ends where you've parked.
  • 09:00–11:00 — Three Distilleries Path, out-and-back Ardbeg → Lagavulin → Ardbeg (~3 miles return, flat, ~2 hrs with stops). Walk west from Ardbeg along the coast path to Lagavulin and back the same way — a walk past the distillery, not a tour of it — ending back at your car at Ardbeg.
  • 11:00–11:10 — Drive Ardbeg → Kildalton (~10 min east along the coast road).
  • 11:10–12:10 — Kildalton Cross & Port Mor walk, 2.5 km (1 hr). The early medieval high cross in its churchyard, then the shore path at Port Mor.
  • 12:10–12:20 — Drive back to Lagavulin. 12:20–13:25 — Lunch on site: Orsay Seafood street food at the Lagavulin Festive Weekend, plus the shop (20% off all weekend) and time to park and check in.
  • 13:30–15:00 — Lagavulin Festive Cocktail Experience Booked 1.5 hrs — your one distillery experience of the trip.
  • 15:00–16:00 — Malt Mill Bar for a dram as the light goes, then stay on for live music from Ciara & Shane, 16:30–19:30 in the Malt Mill Bar, with Orsay Seafood street food all day.
  • Evening meal on the way back or at base: book ahead — Bowmore Hotel (17:30–20:30, 01496 810416) or Port Charlotte Hotel (18:00–21:00).

Forecast: rain and wind · 9°C, feels 3°C · rain 70%, 3.9 mm · SSE wind 22 mph · sunrise 08:25, sunset 16:00.

Sunday29 November · west coast or south coast

A full loop: west coast, Port Ellen fair, Gruinart geese at dusk

  • 08:45 — Drive Port Charlotte → Kilchoman (~15 min). 09:00–10:00 — Machir Bay walk, 3.1 km (1 hr): out along the sand and dunes and back from the Kilchoman car park.
  • 10:00–10:25 — Kilchoman café (opens 10:00 on Sunday; open Sun–Tue 10:00–15:30, last food 14:15) — coffee and cake before the drive south. Don't linger: Port Ellen is ~50 min away.
  • 11:15–12:15 — Ramsay Hall Christmas Fair, Port Ellen (1 hr). Craft stalls, gifts and refreshments, run by South Islay Development — it's on today, Sun 11:00–15:00 (some listings say it ends 14:00, another reason to go in this slot, not later).
  • 12:15 — Drive Port Ellen → Gruinart (~40 min). 12:55–13:55 — Lunch at the Islay Oyster Shed, Craigens Farm (lunch 12:00–14:45) — oysters, crab and home baking. Book ahead: 07376 781214.
  • 14:00–15:00 — RSPB Loch Gruinart Woodland Trail, 1 mile (1 hr) — the waymarked loop from the reserve car park, right by the Oyster Shed.
  • 15:00–16:00 — The Gruinart hides for the geese at dusk. Peak season: thousands of Greenland barnacle and white-fronted geese flight in to roost on the flats as the light fails (sunset 15:59) — the best wildlife hour of the weekend, and it only works in this last slot.
  • Evening: Bowmore Christmas lights switch-on, 15:00–17:00, The Square, Bowmore — hot chocolate, waffles, hot dogs and mulled wine, with Santa and elves handing out presents. It overlaps the Gruinart dusk slot above, so it's one or the other: leave Gruinart at 16:00 and you can still catch the last part in Bowmore on the way to supper at the Bowmore Hotel (17:30–20:30) or back in Port Charlotte.

Forecast: showers and wind · 8°C, feels 2°C · rain 50%, 2.9 mm · SSW wind 21 mph · sunrise 08:26, sunset 15:59.

Monday30 November · leave

One proper walk from the door, then the 12:45 ferry

  • 08:45–09:45 — Loch Indaal Way, Port Charlotte → Bruichladdich, 4.5 km (1 hr, one way). The shore path north along Loch Indaal from the village — it starts from your base, so there's no drive first.
  • 09:45–10:15 — Coffee in Bruichladdich, then back to Port Charlotte by pre-booked taxi (10 min) — book the return the day before; don't walk back, there isn't time before the ferry.
  • 10:15–11:00 — Pack, check out, last coffee in Port Charlotte. If you want a final short stop instead of the coffee, Saligo Bay (0.5 miles, ~20 min on the sand) is a 10-min drive west — but only if you're packed first.
  • 11:00 — Leave Port Charlotte for Port Askaig (~1 hr, arrive ~12:00).
  • 12:45 Port Askaig → Kennacraig 14:40 Your sailing — check in by 12:15 with a car, 12:35 on foot.

Forecast: showers and wind · 10°C, feels 4°C · rain 60%, 4.7 mm · S wind 23 mph · sunrise 08:28, sunset 15:58.

What's on this weekend

Everything verified on Islay Info's What's On and the Persabus diary on 24 Nov 2026 — and everything here fits around your days as planned.

Thu 26 – Sat 28 Nov

Lagavulin Festive Weekend

20% shop discount all three days; Orsay Seafood street food Fri & Sat; winter cocktails and drams in the Malt Mill Bar.

Sat 28 Nov · 13:30

Lagavulin Festive Cocktail Experience Booked

Your booking — 1.5 hrs, from £40. Saturday's plan walks the Three Distilleries Path and Kildalton in the morning and gets you there for 13:30. Live music from Ciara & Shane follows in the Malt Mill Bar, 16:30–19:30, with Orsay Seafood street food all day.

More to do — experiences, guiding & workshops

A second, wider search on 24 Nov 2026 — operator sites, RSPB, islayjura.com, community pages and booking platforms. What follows is what is genuinely doable that weekend, including enquiry-only guiding and workshops to arrange ahead.

Guided — by arrangement only

By arrangement · full day 09:30–17:00, half day 10:00–13:30

Islay Outdoors — bespoke guiding

Guided wildlife, birdwatching and archaeology walks, seashore foraging and fishing with DJ MacPhee (STGA Green Badge); also covers Jura. Wildlife / birdwatching from £250 half day / £350 full day, foraging from £300 / £450, fishing from £250 / £350 (1–4 people). No seasonal closure is published, but availability for 26–30 Nov can't be checked online — booking is essential: 01496 850643 / 07985 403537, dj@islayoutdoors.com.

Source: islayoutdoors.com — prices · tours

Half day · by arrangement · winter tour

Islay Encounters — “Wild Goose Chase”

Winter goose driving tour including RSPB Loch Gruinart, with hot drinks, snacks and optics provided. Max 5, minimum age 12; Port Ellen pickup at 09:00 on request. Price and 2026 dates are not published — enquiry only: 07930 054840, info@islayencounters.co.uk.

Source: islayencounters.co.uk — Wild Goose Chase

All year · half day ~3 hrs

FatBike Islay — guided fatbike tour, Port Ellen

Guided beach and otters tour, starting 09:30/10:00 or 13:30/14:00/14:30, sunset rides possible. £55 per person (£60 with the one eFatBike); ages 12+, up to 9 riders. Book ahead: Dave Protherough, 07973 725456, kayakislay@gmail.com.

Source: kayakwildislay.co.uk — FatBike Islay

Self-guided · centre 10:00–17:00 daily

RSPB Loch Gruinart — winter birding

Reserve open 24 hrs, visitor centre and toilets 10:00–17:00 daily, free, no booking. Hides and an observation window over the Gruinart Flats in peak barnacle and white-fronted goose season — already in Sunday's plan at dusk. There are no RSPB guided walks in 2026, so this one is self-guided.

Source: RSPB — Loch Gruinart opening times (verified live 24 Nov 2026)

RSPB Loch Gruinart

Open

Reserve open 24 hrs; visitor centre daily 10:00–17:00. Peak goose season — thousands of Greenland barnacle and white-fronted geese, best watched coming in to roost at dusk.

RSPB The Oa & American Monument

Open access

Reserve open 24 hrs, no visitor centre. 3.5 km circular trail from Upper Killeyan car park via the monument, 1–1.5 hrs. Cliffs ~100 m — keep well back, especially in high wind.

Kildalton Cross

Open, free

Year-round, Historic Environment Scotland. Pairs with the Three Distilleries Path on the south coast.

Bowmore Round Church

Open daily

Open daily in Nov

10:00–16:00, about 2 miles from Port Charlotte — farm meat, deli, preserves, wool and tweed gifts. One source says Wed–Sun.

Open Thu, Sat & Sun

25 m pool, gym and 5-seat eco sauna. Tue–Fri 12:30–20:00, Sat 10:00–17:00, Sun 10:30–17:30; closed Mon. Swim £5.80, swim + sauna £7.50.

Eat & drink

Near your base in Port Charlotte, plus Bowmore and the places the days take you past. November is quiet — book evening meals.

Port Charlotte Hotel

Main Street, Port Charlotte — open all year to non-residents. Lunch 12:00–14:00, evening meals 18:00–21:00. Bar with Islay malts, Islay Ales on tap and a wood-burning fire. Small dining room, so book: 01496 850360.

Lochindaal Hotel, Port Charlotte

Two bars on the same street as the Port Charlotte Hotel: a large rare-malt collection, log burners and a dog-friendly public bar with pool and darts.

Bowmore Hotel & Lucci's Whisky Bar

Jamieson Street, Bowmore. Lunch 12:00–14:30, evening 17:30–20:30. Lucci's holds 1,300+ single malts — the island's big whisky bar. Book: 01496 810416.

Islay Oyster Shed, Craigens Farm, Gruinart

Oysters, crab sandwiches and home baking by the RSPB reserve. Listings disagree on the days — all agree Sat and Sun are open, and Sunday's plan has lunch there 12:55–13:55; Thu 26 and Mon 30 are disputed. Book ahead: 07376 781214.

Windswept Farm Shop, Tormisdale

On the Port Charlotte–Kilchoman side of the island, 10:00–16:00 daily in November: farm meat, deli, preserves and wool / tweed gifts. An easy stop on the way to or from Machir Bay.

Islay Ales tap room, Glenegedale

Opposite the airport, Mon–Sat 10:00–17:30 with draft beer 11:00–17:15, Sun closed. Pints at the bar only — skip the £19.95 brewery tour, which includes a whisky tasting on top of your Lagavulin booking.

Lagavulin Malt Mill Bar

Open across the Festive Weekend for winter cocktails and drams, with Orsay Seafood street food on Fri & Sat — handy before or after your Saturday experience.

On Jura (Friday)

Lunch in Friday's plan: The Antlers Bakehouse & Bar in Craighouse is open Tue–Sun; the Jura Hotel pub opens Thu–Sat in November (food times are posted on the pub's Facebook page). Lussa Gin's shop is up at Ardlussa, ~25 miles north of the Feolin ferry — Friday's north-road drive passes it for a brief shop stop (no tour).

Sources: Port Charlotte Hotel · Lochindaal Hotel · Bowmore Hotel · Persabus dining · isleofjura.scot — eat & drink

Walks & wildlife

The non-distillery core of the trip — these are the walks timed into the days above. Distances and durations from Walkhighlands / Islay Info.

3.1 KM · 1 HR · SUNDAY 09:00

Machir Bay

Sand and dunes at Kilchoman, car park close by — out along the beach and back in the hour. Straight into Kilchoman café (opens 10:00 Sunday) afterwards in Sunday's plan.

0.5 MILES · VERY EASY

Saligo Bay

Dunes, famous light and the “Sleeping Giant” rock to the north. Best at sunset — which conveniently falls around 16:00. Parking is limited.

1 MILE · 1 HR · SUNDAY 14:00, HIDES AT DUSK

Loch Gruinart Woodland Trail & geese

The waymarked woodland loop (1 mile, 1 hr) from the RSPB car park, then the hides: November is peak goose season, thousands of Greenland barnacle and white-fronted geese returning to roost on the flats at dusk. Also hen harrier, peregrine, teal and wigeon. Timed as Sunday's last two hours, after lunch at the Oyster Shed next door.

~3 MILES RETURN · SAT 09:00 · KILDALTON 2.5 KM · 1 HR · SAT 11:10

Three Distilleries Path & Kildalton Cross

Saturday morning in the plan: drive to Ardbeg and park there, then walk out-and-back Ardbeg → Lagavulin → Ardbeg along the coast — a walk past the distillery rather than a tour of it — ending back at the car. Then drive east to the Kildalton Cross, one of Scotland's finest early medieval crosses, with the Port Mor shore walk (2.5 km, 1 hr), and drive back to Lagavulin in time for the 13:30 booking.

3.5 KM · CIRCULAR · 1–1.5 HRS

Mull of Oa & the American Monument

RSPB circular trail from Upper Killeyan car park. Golden eagles, choughs and twite, grey seals below ~100 m cliffs. Keep well back from the edges, especially in the forecast wind. The spare half-day walk if Saturday's weather kills the south-coast plan — it's the same corner of the island as Lagavulin.

4 KM · 1 HR 15 MIN · FRIDAY 11:00

Corran Sands, Jura

Friday's main walk: the shore-and-river loop from Big Corran, just north of Craighouse — white sand and Paps views, back in Craighouse for the pier stops and lunch.

2.5 KM · 1 HR · PORTNAHAVEN & PORT WEMYSS

The Rhinns villages

The linked harbour villages at the tip of the Rhinns — whitewashed cottages, the harbour at Portnahaven and views across to Orsay and the Rhinns lighthouse. An easy shore wander from Port Charlotte when you have an hour to spare.

4.5 KM · 1 HR ONE WAY · MONDAY 08:45

Loch Indaal Way — Port Charlotte → Bruichladdich

Monday's walk in the plan: the shore path north from Port Charlotte to Bruichladdich, one hour one way, with a pre-booked taxi back (10 min) in time to pack and leave for the 12:45 ferry.

Stay out of the water at Machir Bay and Saligo Bay.

Both have strong currents and rip currents and are not suitable for swimming. The Atlantic surf on the west coast is powerful: check tides before exploring rocks or headlands (the tide can cut off your return), there are no lifeguards, and in a coastal emergency call 999 and ask for the Coastguard. Deer stalking season runs to 15 February on Jura and Islay — the Corran Sands walk keeps to the shore and is fine, but check with estates before going off-road. On Islay, buses stop early (last buses ~17:12–18:26) and there are no buses on Sundays, so a car is effectively essential and taxis need booking well ahead.

Sources: Islay Info walks · Islay Info — Atlantic coast · Hidden Scotland — Corran Sands · Garelochhead Coaches — bus 456

Check before you go

Things the research (done 24 Nov 2026) couldn't pin down — worth a look or a phone call nearer the day.

  • CalMac service status on both travel mornings. No disruption was showing on 24 Nov, but November weather cancels sailings at short notice — especially with Thursday night's forecast. Check the route page.
  • No booking needed for the Jura ferry on Friday — it's turn-up-and-go. 10:30 out, 17:45 back.
  • Book the Jura sauna. Bothan Jura Wild Sauna, Big Corran / Craighouse — Friday 16:00 slot: confirm it's bookable and booked before you go; Friday's plan has a fallback hour if it isn't.
  • Book Monday's taxi back from Bruichladdich (for ~10:00) the day before — the Loch Indaal Way walk is one-way in the plan, and there's no slack before the 12:45 ferry.
  • Guided options are enquiry-only. Islay Outdoors (01496 850643 / dj@islayoutdoors.com) and Islay Encounters' Wild Goose Chase (07930 054840, price not published) publish no availability for 26–30 Nov — phone or email before you go if you want either. Same for FatBike Islay (07973 725456) and Tideline workshops (07845 036456).
  • Book Persabus Pottery ahead if you want the Sat 28 Nov 12:00 session — November–March sessions must be booked in advance (01496 840243), and it's tight before Lagavulin at 13:30.
  • MacTaggart Leisure Centre session times vary — the centre is open Thu, Sat and Sun that weekend (closed Mon), but check the pool / sauna session times before setting off (01496 810767).
  • Islay Oyster Shed days are disputed — listings disagree on Thu 26 and Mon 30; Sat and Sun are agreed. Confirm when you book on 07376 781214.
